lines: San Francisco is the last unbeaten at 6-0 after holding off Washington 23-17. Jayden Daniels went 29/40 for 300 yards and 2 TD and still lost. They host Atlanta Monday 1:00 am as SF -3.5.
Kansas City sits 5-0 after a 22-6 win over the Chargers, who are 0-6. Kenneth Walker III ran 19 for 128 and 2 TD. Seattle is a 2.5-point home favourite on Monday at 8:20 am.
Pittsburgh needed overtime to beat Tampa 26-19 and is 4-2. They meet the Saints in Paris on Sunday at 9:30 pm, PIT -3.5, total 44.5.
Cleveland beat Baltimore 10-13 the other way: Browns 13, Ravens 10, with Tyler Huntley 19/31, 165 yards, 1 TD. The Browns are only 1.5-point favourites at Tennessee.
Minnesota is 5-0 and lays 6.5 at home to the Colts. Houston, 2-4 after beating Jacksonville 34-31 in London, is a 10-point favourite over the Giants.
Thursday's opener is New England at Chicago, both 4-2, Bears -3 with a 50.5 total, Friday 8:15 am Perth time on Prime Video.

postgame.what_decided_it: Turnovers. Miami outgained Cincinnati 331 to 307 and ran for 217 at 6.4 a pop, but coughed it up three times to the Bengals' one. Burrow turned short fields into four touchdowns.
standouts: Joe Burrow: 23/32, 190 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT. Not a volume day, 5.9 yards per pass, but clean and sharp inside the 20.
Ja'Marr Chase: 6 catches, 77 yards, 1 TD. Still the first read that always works.
Per the ESPN recap headline, Battle had a pair of interceptions. Malik Willis finished 15/27, 137 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT.
postgame.division_meaning: Baltimore sits 4-1 on a W3 run. Cincinnati, Cleveland and Pittsburgh are all 3-2. The Bengals' +19 point differential is second in the North behind the Ravens' +27.
postgame.the_take: A win over an 0-5 team that you got outgained in is not a fix. Ben Baby's piece says the Bengals know they can play better. Giving up 217 on the ground travels badly to Baltimore on Mon, 26 Oct, 1:00 am.
